title: POC Weekly Sync - Dedicated Sizing & Autoscale
summary: Weekly POC sync to review Dedicated pilot results. Discussed 95th p90 latency, throughput variability under business hours, autoscale headroom and burst plan, and security/compliance gating. Agreed to run a 2-hour high-traffic benchmark and adjust autoscale min/max and warm pools. Next: Redwood to send updated pricing, sizing options, and autoscale policy proposal; AtlasPay to provide day-of-week traffic profile and test account for benchmark.
action_items: Maya Patel: Send updated Dedicated pricing + Sizing options by 2025-10-16
Liam Ortega: Prepare benchmark plan and runbook for 2-hour high-traffic test (target week of 10/20)
Sofia Chen: Share 7-day traffic profile CSV and peak QPS by 2025-10-15
Dana Morris: Confirm encryption/KMS scope and sign NDA addendum if needed by 2025-10-20
next_steps: Redwood to schedule 2-hour stress benchmark and invite AtlasPay SREs
AtlasPay to provide traffic traces and sample workload by 10/15
Redwood to propose autoscale policy (min/max nodes, warm pool size, scale-up cooldown) by 10/16
Follow-up sync after benchmark to review logs and tweak policies (tentative 10/23)
transcript:
[15:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — go over last week's results, tuning for dedicated pool, autoscale and burst plan, and next steps.
[15:01] Sofia Chen: yep sounds good, we ran the integration tests overnight, had some odd p90 spikes around 11am-1pm.
[15:02] Liam Ortega: okay can you share the p90 numbers? is that token latency or end-to-end?
[15:03] Sofia Chen: it's end-to-end, so includes our routing, it's around 320-420ms for gen requests normally p95 was 480ms but on the spike it hit 800ms.
[15:04] Maya Patel: got it. that aligns with what we saw in the Redwood Dedicated telemetry, we saw increased queueing when you hit sustained QPS above your baseline.
[15:05] Rajiv Gupta: just to add, our daytime traffic pattern has a big jump at 11:30 for about 25 minutes — it's a batch send from a partner.
[15:06] Hannah Li: okay that's an important pattern, we should tune autoscale to anticipate that predictable surge rather than purely reactive.
[15:07] Ethan Park: quick question — how long does it take to spin up additional GPUs in the Dedicated pool? like a cold scale up.
[15:08] Liam Ortega: if we need fresh nodes it can be 3-7 minutes depending on image pull and model warmup, but with warm pool (pre-warmed instances) we can serve within 30-60s. there was a note in the deck about warm pool sizes.
[15:09] Dana Morris: from a security perspective, we need clarity on KMS integration and audit logs for the warm instances — we don't want keys on nodes that are not registered.
[15:10] Maya Patel: yeah we'll include KMS/KMS key rotation details in the security doc, and warm pool nodes are customer-tenanted and go through the same enrollment flow.
[15:11] Sofia Chen: there were also some artifacts where the KV cache wasn't high hit rate, maybe workbench caching misaligned — sometimes the transcript says K V cash in the logs.
[15:12] Liam Ortega: haha yeah the transcriber loves K V cash. The reality is prefix/KV cache hit rate is low when requests have high variance in prompts. we can look at increasing prefix matching window, or suggest a small prompt normalization step at client side.
[15:13] Rajiv Gupta: what about quantization? we tested INT8 in staging and saw lower latency but small quality regression on a handful of prompts.
[15:14] Hannah Li: exactly — quantization is a tradeoff. For critical payment flows we recommend FP16 or bfloat where possible and reserve INT8 for non-critical workloads. you can also have model variant routing for cost optimization.
[15:15] Maya Patel: on sizing — based on your average QPS and the observed p95, we recommend a base Dedicated pool of 6 x A100-equivalent for steady state with a warm pool of 2 nodes and max of 12 nodes to cover bursts. that's a starting point pending the benchmark.
[15:16] Ethan Park: can you explain the autoscale thresholds you'd recommend?
[15:17] Liam Ortega: sure. baseline: keep min nodes at 6, scale-up trigger when CPU or queue length exceeds 60% for 30s, add nodes in increments of 2, cooldown of 120s; warm pool of 2 to cut cold-starts. for bursting beyond max, we can route to a lower-cost hosted fallback model but only if that's acceptable for data residency.
[15:18] Dana Morris: fallback to hosted is a non-starter unless we have a contractual data handling guarantee. At a minimum we need encryption in transit + at rest, and SSO access controls.
[15:19] Maya Patel: understood, we can make fallback opt-in and only to redwood-hosted variants if you permit data residency or to a private-hosted standby in your VPC.
[15:20] Sofia Chen: what's the expected cost delta for warm pool and larger max nodes? we need to justify it to finance.
[15:21] Maya Patel: warm pool adds nominal cost — roughly equivalent to 2 nodes running idle; but it saves you on the cost of failed requests and latency SLO breaches. we'll provide a cost/latency tradeoff spreadsheet after the call.
[15:22] Liam Ortega: also remember batching helps — if your traffic allows 20–40ms added latency we can batch to improve throughput and lower per-token cost. but for low-latency payment auth flows we keep batching minimal.
[15:23] Rajiv Gupta: what about scaling cooldowns, sometimes we see thrash where it scales up and down rapidly.
[15:24] Hannah Li: use a combination of integrated metrics: require both queue length > threshold and sustained CPU > threshold for scale-up; and use a longer cooldown for scale-down, like 5–10 minutes. that reduces oscillation.
[15:25] Ethan Park: for the benchmark, do you want us to run production traffic replay or synthetic load?
[15:26] Liam Ortega: production replay is best for cache behavior, but synthetic allows higher peak control. recommended: 1-hour replay followed by a 2-hour synthetic spike to validate burst handling.
[15:27] Sofia Chen: we'll try to provide a scrubbed replay trace that removes PII.
[15:28] Dana Morris: confirm again SLA targets — can Redwood hit 99.9% availability and p95 < 500ms for our critical endpoints?
[15:29] Maya Patel: SLA targets we can commit to in Dedicated contracts for uptime; performance SLOs we'll work towards and include in the pilot acceptance criteria — the benchmark will be the acceptance gate for p95 goals.
[15:30] Rajiv Gupta: ok let's talk timeline, we can provide traces by 10/15, run benchmark 10/21, and sync 10/23.
[15:31] Maya Patel: sounds good. i'll send updated pricing and the autoscale policy doc by 10/16, liam will share the benchmark runbook and invite.
[15:32] Liam Ortega: i'll also include the steps to increase prefix/KV cache match window and a quick script for prompt normalization to help hit cache rates.
[15:33] Hannah Li: small note — we should test quantized variant routing in the benchmark but keep critical flows on fp16.
[15:34] Sofia Chen: agreed. any other blocking items?
[15:35] Dana Morris: I need the KMS integration diagram and audit log retention policy; otherwise we're fine to proceed with tests pending legal sign-off.
[15:36] Maya Patel: we'll attach the security diagram and SOC2 attestation in the follow-up email.
[15:37] Ethan Park: great, thanks everyone.
[15:38] Maya Patel: recap of next steps: Redwood sends pricing + autoscale policy + benchmark plan; AtlasPay provides traces and signs NDA addendum if required; run benchmark and reconvene. Thanks all.
[15:39] Sofia Chen: thanks, bye.
